purpose: Owner request: carry the release-3 towns into the downstream layers (reach, trade, administration).
principle: Mechanical reruns of the existing, already Earth-tested downstream rules with ONE input changed: the unmarked towns (and the tracks that follow from them). No downstream parameter is refitted and no new Earth claim is made. polity.release3_placement routes the standard placement call to the reviewed release-3 positions and refuses any other input.
control: For each climate the unmodified exporter runs in the same kind of staging atlas and its layer images are compared byte for byte with the published ones. If they differ, the difference is reported and the release-3 layers are compared against that control, not presented as exact like-for-like.
stage_1_reach_and_trade: polity.export on staging copies for raw and corrected climate: effective control, hardest-month control, months within a day, days beyond the roads, days from the capital, what closes the roads, who reaches where, sailing, trade and market views. Published as the displayed version of those layers through a layer manifest read by the page; atlas.json, release.json and every published legacy file stay byte-identical.
stage_2_administration: Rerun the imperial access audit (six source cases, both climates) on release-3 towns and tracks and publish beside the earlier audit.
stage_3_supply_supported_reach: The default supply-supported reach (control v2.1) sits on the chain market hinterlands -> joint food budget -> field work -> fertility -> control v2 -> v2.1. Rerun with release-3 POSITIONS and the chain's original 7.5% civilian request, because that request is part of the rule that was blind-tested on Earth; feeding the release-2 calibrated residents into it would be a new, untested model and is a separate decision. Attempted after stages 1-2; if it cannot be completed in this session it is reported as open, with what blocks it.
town_sizes: Release-2/3 residents do not enter reach, trade or administration in this step except where the existing rule already reads town positions. Trade's market masses come from hinterland people, not the calibrated residents.
review: Controls as above; summary statistics of every changed layer against its legacy version; browser check; checkout check.

amendments.owner_decision: Use one third of surplus marketed and feed the calibrated residents into the reach chain.
amendments.rule: A town is a staffed source for the control rule when it has a polity affiliation and its supply-fed residents (release-3 sliding-density residents x fed share from the wide grain supply scenario, one third marketed, labour-limited production) reach the chain's own threshold of 150 (100 institutional + 50 civilians). This replaces the chain's local food budget with its 7.5% request for deciding which towns are staffed. The control rule itself (v2: staffed sites plus roads within two days; v2.1 geography) is unchanged.
amendments.status: The control rule was blind-tested on Earth with the earlier staffing input, so this map rests on the rule's tests plus an untested supply scenario. Both earlier release-3 versions (7.5% request) stay published.
amendments.known_before: Wide supply results: 1,012 of 1,053 corrected towns fully fed, 41 short but partly fed; every town's fed residents exceed 150, so staffing will differ from the 7.5% chain only where that chain's local food test failed.
